A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mentor/SuperMentor study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original error-prediction experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1K, colorectal histology and additional ImageNet OOD datasets, including ablations and generalization analyses.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark results and supplementary experiments, including weight-perturbation analyses and a breakdown of errors shared across mentee architectures.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces L = Ld + Lr with L = alpha Lr + (1-alpha) Ld, where alpha = (n/N)^q varies across training epochs. This changes the training objective through a weighting schedule; the two-stream architecture and ViT/PIFGSM SuperMentor design remain.

E1.justification: V3 expands the ImageNet baseline evaluation to multiple corruption and attack severities, broadening the tested input conditions beyond the default strengths. The datasets and tasks remain: colorectal histology and the five additional ImageNet OOD datasets already appeared in v2. The natural-adversarial analysis partitions existing ImageNet samples rather than introducing another dataset.

E2.justification: The corresponding ImageNet and medical comparisons retain SER, MCP, CPE, DTC, ConfidNet, TrustScore and SSL. The appendix also retains the same MCP, CPE and DTC threshold configurations. Revised scores and the changed strongest baseline do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: V2's per-error-source balanced test sampling is replaced by a 70/30 partition of original images, explicitly keeping their modified versions within the same partition. Training changes from 40 to 30 epochs, with revised learning rates and batch sizes. V3 also introduces multi-severity baseline evaluation and changes the loss ablation from ViT SuperMentor with a ResNet50 mentee to ResNet50 mentors with ViT mentees. These are reported protocol changes, not merely additional disclosure.

E4.justification: V3 adds two weight-perturbation analyses testing error-source and backbone effects, an all-nine-source joint-training experiment, and shared-versus-architecture-specific error analysis. Existing loss ablations are revised under different model configurations; EigenCAM examples change from Gaussian blur to spatter. Detailed transfer tables disappear, although the generalization experiment and summary plot remain.

E5.justification: V3 adds ANOVA and two-tailed t-tests supporting the error-source comparisons, reporting p-values below 0.05, and introduces three-run uncertainty reporting for the main baseline comparison in Figure 6(a). V2 already reported three-run standard deviations for ablations and appendix results, so this is an expansion of statistical reporting, not evidence of an increased run count.

E6.justification: Results change throughout the plots and tables. V2 Table 1 reports SuperMentor at 77.0% versus the strongest baseline, MCP, at 74.7%; v3 Figure 6(a) reports 70.4% versus SSL at 66.7% under revised training and multi-severity evaluation. These are not same-setting performance changes. Joint-training, medical and additional OOD scores also change, new diagnostic results appear, and detailed transfer entries from v2 Tables S6-S8 are removed.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 introduces the mathematical weighting function alpha = (n/N)^q and changes the defined total objective accordingly. The error-prediction target and component-loss definitions remain; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: small-perturbation adversarial training supports error prediction, transformer mentors perform better, mentors transfer across mentee architectures, and SuperMentor outperforms the baseline methods overall. Additional analyses support these retained claims.

C2.justification: V3's joint-training discussion acknowledges the 21,000-versus-7,000 training-sample difference and interprets all-source training as an empirical upper-bound comparison. It also links wider mentor loss landscapes to generalizable features and identifies shared errors as one explanation for transfer. The mentor-vulnerability arguments largely persist through relocation into Section 4.5.

D1.justification: V3 replaces the promised future release with a code/data hyperlink, documents q values and revised hardware and training settings, and gives joint-training sample counts. V2's detailed per-source split-count table is removed in favor of the common split description. The PDFs establish the access statement and link, not the external resource's actual availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds Li et al. (2018), Visualizing the Loss Landscape of Neural Nets, and Hendrycks et al. (2021b), Natural Adversarial Examples, to motivate its added analyses. The broader positioning remains stable. Numerous other reference changes update publication metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: Section 4.5 is reframed around mentor analysis, existing ablation and vulnerability discussions move into the main text, and the appendices are reorganized. Terminology, affiliations, publication text and acknowledgements also change. Most introductory prose and the overall main-section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 combines the main baseline summary, revised ablation and EigenCAM visualization in Figure 6, and separates Figure 4's overlaid curves into panels. It adds two loss-landscape figures and a shared-error table, redraws the embedding plots, and removes the split-count and detailed transfer tables. These substantially reorganize the visual presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens evaluation clarity through explicit image-disjoint splitting and supports the central findings with broader severity testing, statistical tests and targeted generalization analyses. These benefits are tempered by removal of detailed transfer tables and a numerical inconsistency in new Table S3: the CW N2 count 977/1952 implies about 50.1%, but 61.4% is printed. Overall, the evidence supports a limited quality improvement; changed performance numbers alone do not establish improvement because the method and settings also change.
